subject.title: [MiniMax] M3 native video input support with timestamp-scaling metadata hint (reference branch only)

question: Should OpenClaw add MiniMax M3 native video through a provider-owned media-understanding path, a new core/session VideoContent tool contract, or defer it behind the generic direct-video tracker?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation choice controls raw-media egress policy, provider capability contracts, prompt/session semantics, and public content types that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Stage Provider-Owned MiniMax Video First
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped MiniMax M3 video path with explicit security limits and metadata handling, while keeping generic readVideo/VideoContent as a separate maintainer-approved design.

options.title: Design Generic Direct Video First
options.body: Use #27482 to define the core chat/tool/session video contract before adopting MiniMax-specific behavior into provider code.

options.title: Keep As Reference Research
options.body: Leave the issue open only as provider research until more MiniMax and cross-provider live proof justifies product work.

recommendation.title: Stage Provider-Owned MiniMax Video First
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly scoped MiniMax M3 video path with explicit security limits and metadata handling, while keeping generic readVideo/VideoContent as a separate maintainer-approved design.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history points to MiniMax M3/provider ownership and maintainer routing near the files this decision would change.
